page: OVHcloud t1-le-180 is a GPU-accelerated server belonging to the Cloud GPU family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by Intel Xeon Silver 4214 processors running at 3.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 180.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.62 GB per core. For acceleration, it bundles four NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs delivering a combined 64 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. Single-core CPU performance is weak, with Geekbench single-core scores in the bottom 10% and stress-ng single-core performance in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance rises to the average tier, supported by the 32 dedicated physical cores. In contrast, the server excels in LLM inference benchmarks. It achieves top-tier results in prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and large models, demonstrating the high parallel processing efficiency of the quad-GPU configuration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the t1-le-180 offers high resource density by bundling four enterprise-grade GPUs with a substantial memory footprint and dedicated CPU resources. This configuration is highly cost-effective for workloads that can leverage parallel GPU execution to offset the lower single-core CPU performance. It is primarily suited for deep learning, large language model inference, data science pipelines, and parallelized scientific computing, while being less optimal for single-threaded application hosting or CPU-bound sequential processing.
